summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across the 3-node Alpine cluster: node1 is the writable primary, node2 and node3 are read-only standbys built via pg_basebackup with a dedicated scram-sha-256 'replicator' role. Verified writes on node1 propagate to both standbys and that standbys reject writes. Performed the mandatory sequential restart protocol (baseline -> reboot -> boot_id change proof -> recovery/replication proof) on all three nodes, one at a time, preserving the primary/standby topology and data integrity throughout.
actions_performed: Inspected all 3 nodes: confirmed plain Alpine Linux 3.23 with no PostgreSQL preinstalled
Installed postgresql16 + postgresql16-contrib via apk on node1, node2, node3
Initialized primary data directory on node1 with initdb (data checksums enabled)

Configured node1 postgresql.conf (listen_addresses='*', wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders=10, max_replication_slots=10, hot_standby=on) and pg_hba.conf (scram-sha-256 rules for replication and normal connections from the cluster subnet)
Started PostgreSQL on node1 and created a 'replicator' ROLE WITH REPLICATION LOGIN using a locally-generated random password (never placed literally in command text)

Distributed the replication password to node2/node3 over the private cluster network using a temporary socat TCP relay (avoided root-SSH, which was blocked by locked root account/PAM), then tore down the relay
Wiped standby data dirs and ran pg_basebackup -R (creates standby.signal + primary_conninfo automatically) from node1 to node2 and node3, using a postgres-owned .pgpass for authentication
Started PostgreSQL on node2 and node3 as standbys; verified pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both streaming, and pg_is_in_recovery()=true on both standbys
Functionally validated replication: created repl_test table + inserted row on node1, confirmed visible on node2/node3, confirmed INSERT rejected on both standbys (read-only)
Enabled postgresql (and confirmed sshd) in the default OpenRC runlevel on all nodes for restart persistence

Executed mandatory restart protocol sequentially: captured boot_id + replication/data baseline on node1, restarted it via 'reboot', polled until reachable, confirmed changed boot_id, confirmed postgresql auto-started and both standbys reconnected/streaming with data intact, then inserted a post-restart row
Repeated the same baseline -> restart -> boot_id-change -> recovery verification sequence for node2, then node3, confirming quorum-independent standby-by-standby restart with no primary disruption
Final cross-node check confirming a newly inserted row on the primary replicated to both node2 and node3 after all three restarts

evidence.requirement: PostgreSQL primary configured on node1 with replication-enabled settings and replication role
evidence.summary: initdb on node1, postgresql.conf/pg_hba.conf updated for wal_level=replica and scram-sha-256 replication access, postgresql started, replicator role created with REPLICATION LOGIN

evidence.requirement: node2 and node3 provisioned as read-only standbys via pg_basebackup from node1
evidence.summary: pg_basebackup -R completed 100% on both nodes creating standby.signal and primary_conninfo pointing at node1; postgresql started successfully on both

evidence.requirement: Standbys are in streaming replication and read-only
evidence.summary: pg_stat_replication on node1 shows both node2 and node3 in 'streaming' state; pg_is_in_recovery() returns true on both standbys

evidence.requirement: Changes committed on the primary are visible on both standbys
evidence.summary: Row inserted on node1 is immediately visible via SELECT on node2 and node3; direct INSERT attempts on both standbys fail with 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction'

evidence.requirement: Credentials generated on managed nodes, not exposed as literals in tool commands
evidence.summary: Replication password generated on node1 via /dev/urandom, used only through shell variable indirection in commands, and relayed to node2/node3 over a temporary socat TCP listener on the private cluster network rather than embedding the literal secret in any tool call; relay torn down afterward

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: baseline capture, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a50ee593... with healthy replication/data captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 2f804993... (changed) confirmed reachable; postgresql auto-started, repl_test data intact, both standbys reconnected streaming

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: baseline capture, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id a03569af... with pg_is_in_recovery=true and data present captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 599f9606... (changed) confirmed reachable; postgresql auto-started in recovery mode with data intact; node1 pg_stat_replication shows node2 reconnected streaming

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: baseline capture, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8b1bd118... with pg_is_in_recovery=true and data present captured; reboot acknowledged; post-restart boot_id 61a998bd... (changed) confirmed reachable; postgresql auto-started in recovery mode with data intact; node1 pg_stat_replication shows both standbys streaming again

evidence.requirement: Post-restart end-to-end replication proof across all three restarted nodes
evidence.summary: A row inserted on node1 after all three restarts appears identically on both node2 and node3, confirming replication remained fully functional through the entire restart sequence
